faq.q: How is the Olympic flame lit?
faq.a: At Olympia in Greece, a curved mirror called a parabolic mirror focuses sunlight onto a torch until it catches fire. This is done months before each Games.
asks: Where is the Olympic flame lit?

faq.q: Why is there an Olympic torch relay?
faq.a: The relay carries a message of peace and friendship from ancient Olympia to the new host, and lets thousands of ordinary people share in the Games.
asks: What does the torch relay mean?

faq.q: Does the Olympic flame ever go out?
faq.a: Sometimes a torch blows out, but backup flames lit from the same fire are always kept in safety lanterns, so it can be relit from the original flame.
asks: What happens if the torch goes out?

faq.q: When did the torch relay start?
faq.a: A flame first burned at the Amsterdam Games in 1928. The first relay from Olympia was for the Berlin Games in 1936.
It is a big bowl or sculpture lit with the flame at the opening ceremony. It burns until the closing ceremony.

facts: The Olympic flame is lit at Olympia, Greece, using a parabolic mirror to focus the Sun's rays.
The first Olympic torch relay from Olympia took place for the 1936 Berlin Games.
